evals.prompt: I'm starting a new Tailwind v4 + React project for a SaaS dashboard. Small team (3 devs), no Figma, no React Native. Our brand color is #6366f1 (indigo). Set up a proper design token system with dark mode support. Give me the complete tokens.css and app.css files ready to drop in.
evals.expected_output: Complete tokens.css with OKLCH primitives + shadcn-style semantic tokens + .dark block, plus app.css with @custom-variant dark, @theme for fonts, @theme inline for utility mappings. Should include the brand indigo color converted to OKLCH and mapped to --primary/--accent. Should explain the @theme vs @theme inline distinction.
expectations: Uses OKLCH color format for primitive colors (not hex or hsl)
Has a two-tier structure: primitive vars (like --indigo-500) and semantic vars (like --primary, --background)
tokens.css has a .dark {} block for future dark-mode overrides
app.css uses @theme inline (not plain @theme) to map semantic vars into Tailwind utilities
Produces bg-background, bg-card, bg-muted, text-foreground, text-muted-foreground, border-border utilities
Explains the @theme vs @theme inline distinction or why @theme inline is used

evals.prompt: We have a Tailwind v4 project with tokens like --color-bg-primary (dark page bg), --color-bg-secondary (card bg), --color-text-default (main text), --color-text-muted (dimmer text), --color-border-ui (dividers). Components use classes like bg-bg-primary, text-text-default, border-border-ui. Help me migrate to shadcn-style naming conventions so the token names are more standard and AI coding tools generate correct code.
evals.expected_output: A concrete migration plan with: new tokens.css using shadcn vocabulary (--background, --card, --foreground, --muted-foreground, --border), the @theme inline block in app.css, and a sed/search-replace guide for renaming the Tailwind utility classes in components. Should warn about the word-boundary double-transformation bug.
expectations: Maps old names to new shadcn names (--background, --foreground, --card, --muted, --muted-foreground, --border)
Provides the new tokens.css structure with semantic :root block
Provides the @theme inline block mapping semantics to --color-* utilities
Includes guidance on renaming classes in components (sed commands or equivalent)
Warns about the word-boundary bug when using sed on inline style CSS vars

evals.prompt: Can you explain the difference between @theme and @theme inline in Tailwind v4? I'm trying to set up dark mode and I'm confused about which one to use. Someone told me @theme inline breaks dark mode but I'm also seeing it used in shadcn/ui which has working dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Clear explanation of the distinction: @theme generates utilities that reference var(--color-*), @theme inline 'inlines' the value. When the inlined value is var(--semantic-name), the utility directly references that var — dark mode works because the browser resolves it at render time. The @theme inline breaks pattern for dark mode is only when you inline literal values (like oklch(...)) directly, not var() references. Also covers the calc() gotcha for derived tokens.
expectations: Correctly explains that plain @theme generates var(--color-*) references in utilities
Correctly explains that @theme inline with a var() value still works for dark mode (resolves at render time)
Explains the calc() gotcha: calc() expressions in @theme inline are evaluated at build time so runtime --radius overrides won't cascade
Gives a concrete example showing the shadcn pattern and why it works
Recommends @theme inline for semantic tokens from :root/.dark, plain @theme for font/spacing primitives
